record.title: Synchronous completion grows the kernel stack
record.observation: Inline completion reentered the provider while earlier frames remained on the kernel stack. Deferring completion through an existing kernel thread-call mechanism allowed the unchanged one-sector diagnostic to finish 39 reads.
record.limits: This early read-only diagnostic had one pending slot and does not validate the later writable queue under saturation.

records.access: Private project record; original material is not distributed

exhibits.title: Same one-sector limit; different completion lifetime
rows: While earlier frames remain on the stack
exhibits.interpretation: Increasing transfer size would hide the recursion depth. Deferral changes the lifetime of the stack frames while preserving the one-sector diagnostic.

excerpts.content:
The first implementation completed reads synchronously. It read sectors 0–16 correctly, but the driver's next-chunk callback reentered the provider before prior frames unwound. The next request faulted at the kernel-stack boundary. Increasing transfer size would only change the depth, so the adapter instead queues successful completions on one preallocated XNU thread call. Each worker snapshots callback arguments before releasing the pending slot. Reentrant requests can queue the next callback without retaining the previous transfer stack.

[…]

The unchanged one-sector request limit then completed 39 reads with no panic or Undefined Instruction exception. The 98 previously observed page-stepping Data Aborts remained; their cause is still unresolved.
